_about: LABELED STARTER SET for T12 (model selection). Each posting is written in natural hiring language (original text, not a verbatim real posting, to avoid reproducing copyrighted material). 'expected' is the set of framework leaf items a human reader says the posting describes, by slug, independent of what the matcher predicts. Labels are best-judgment ground truth pending Morgan's review. Labeling convention: an activity is labeled when the posting describes DOING the work; a deliverable when it names the ARTIFACT produced; a tool when it is named. Paraphrase is deliberate, so the keyword baseline will miss items the LLM step should catch. See README 'Fixtures'.
_labeling_rule: Named-artifact rule (guidance for human labelers, NOT enforced by code): map each posting phrase to EVERY framework deliverable it names or refers to as a noun. A single phrase can carry several deliverables (for example 'annotated designs' -> design-annotation AND high-fidelity-prototypes). Do NOT label a deliverable when only the producing activity is described and no artifact noun is referred to (for example 'call out risks' is the activity analyzing-project-risk, not a risk-analysis deliverable). Borderline cases are a recorded human judgment call. The recognizer already returns multiple items per quote and the scorer counts per slug, so many-deliverables-per-phrase needs no engine change. The eval validates that every expected slug EXISTS in the framework, but never decides what should be labeled.
_scope: A strong-match posting for all eleven covered job functions, plus a title-fit mismatch and a not-covered title (both unscored). Expand with more postings per function before trusting the aggregate numbers; the set is still small, so run-to-run variance is not yet characterized.
